game: Super Mario Bros. / Super Mario Bros. Deluxe (GBC)
note: See roster.md for per-fact confidence markers ([verified]/[inferred]/[must-verify]) and full citation context. size_px marked null where no source gave a measurable dimension; size_tiles is inferred from the 8x8 NES/GBC tile grid unless stated.

entities.name: Mario (Small)
entities.behavior: Player character in base form. Dies in one hit from any enemy contact. Can break bricks from below only while running/jumping as an adult form, not while small.
entities.palette_notes: GBC recolor of the NES red/blue overalls scheme; exact SMBD palette indices not sourced.

entities.name: Mario (Super)
entities.behavior: Grown form after collecting a Super Mushroom. Survives one hit by shrinking back to Small Mario instead of dying. Can break brick blocks from below.

entities.name: Mario (Fire)
entities.behavior: Grown form after collecting a Fire Flower. Can throw up to 2 fireballs on screen at once via the B button; reverts directly to Small Mario if hit (no cushioning step in SMB1/SMBD).
entities.palette_notes: White/black outfit recolor in NES original; SMBD GBC palette not sourced.

entities.name: Luigi
entities.behavior: Second player character, identical hitbox and physics to Mario in the SMB1/SMBD era; distinguished by palette only (this era predates Luigi's distinct taller/thinner model).
entities.palette_notes: Green recolor of the Mario sprite.

entities.name: Goomba
entities.behavior: Walks back and forth and attacks by walking/charging into Mario. Falls off ledges without turning. Its 'walk' is animated by flipping between two mirrored sprite states rather than distinct walk frames.
entities.palette_notes: Gray in NES original; SMBD modernizes the palette (exact values not sourced).

entities.name: Koopa Troopa (Green)
entities.behavior: Walks in a straight line and falls off ledges without turning. Stomping forces it into its shell, which can then be kicked to slide into other enemies or blocks.

entities.name: Koopa Troopa (Red)
entities.behavior: Turns around at ledges instead of walking off ('timid' per the original manual). Otherwise identical shell/stomp mechanics to the green variant.

entities.name: Koopa Shell (state)
entities.behavior: Result of stomping a Koopa Troopa or Paratroopa. Sits still until kicked, then slides at speed along the floor, destroying enemies and breakable blocks it hits, until it strikes a wall or is stopped.
entities.palette_notes: Matches the parent Koopa's shell color.

entities.name: Koopa Paratroopa (Green)
entities.behavior: Winged Koopa Troopa. Bounces toward the player or flies back and forth horizontally. Stomping removes its wings, converting it into a regular green Koopa Troopa.

entities.name: Koopa Paratroopa (Red)
entities.behavior: Winged Koopa Troopa that flies up and down along a fixed vertical path. Stomping removes its wings, converting it into a regular red Koopa Troopa.

entities.name: Buzzy Beetle
entities.behavior: Hard-shelled Koopa variant that walks toward the player and off ledges without turning, like a green Koopa Troopa. Immune to fireballs due to its hard shell; can be kicked as a shell once stomped.

entities.name: Spiny
entities.behavior: Spike-shelled Koopa hatched from a Spiny Egg. Walks toward the player. Cannot be safely stomped (jumping on it damages Mario instead); must be defeated with a fireball or Starman.

entities.name: Spiny Egg
entities.behavior: Thrown straight downward by a Lakitu in the original SMB1/SMBD (no arc trajectory). Hatches into a walking Spiny on ground contact. Lakitu throws 1 egg if Mario is Small, 2 if Super/Fire.
entities.palette_notes: Spiked, red/orange, smaller than a hatched Spiny.

entities.name: Lakitu
entities.behavior: Rides a small white cloud above the action, hides for about 1 second before dropping a Spiny Egg straight down. Retreats offscreen automatically as the player nears the flagpole. Respawns after several seconds if defeated.
entities.palette_notes: Ring-patterned shell, distinct from other Koopas' hex pattern.

entities.name: Hammer Bro
entities.behavior: Taller upright Koopa that hops continuously (nearly as high as Mario) and throws hammers at the player, using a low/far or high/close arc depending on distance. Depicted without shoes in the SMB1/SMBD era.
entities.palette_notes: Yellow body, green shell and helmet.

entities.name: Bullet Bill
entities.behavior: Self-propelled projectile enemy that flies in a straight line, ignoring gravity, after being fired from a Bill Blaster.

entities.name: Bill Blaster (launcher)
entities.behavior: Stationary cannon that periodically fires Bullet Bills. Will not fire while the player is directly above it or in the sprite box immediately adjacent to it. Indestructible in SMB1/SMBD.

entities.name: Cheep-Cheep (Red)
entities.behavior: Faster of the two Cheep-Cheep colors. In lava-level contexts, leaps up from the bottom of the screen toward the player.

entities.name: Cheep-Cheep (Grey)
entities.behavior: Slower of the two Cheep-Cheep colors. Swims through underwater level sections rather than leaping.
entities.confidence: verified behavior / underwater-stomp rule unverified for SMB1

entities.name: Blooper
entities.behavior: Small squid enemy that cannot touch the ground; follows the player through water in a zig-zag swimming pattern.
entities.palette_notes: SMBD recolors it off-white, vs. tan/brown in the NES original and pink in Super Mario All-Stars.
entities.confidence: verified behavior / stomp rule unverified for SMB1

entities.name: Podoboo
entities.behavior: Fireball that periodically jumps out of lava pits in a simple pattern to attack the player. Completely invincible in the original SMB1 — cannot be defeated by any means.
entities.palette_notes: Orange/red fireball with a simple face.

entities.name: Fire Bar (short)
entities.behavior: Rotating obstacle made of about 6 fireball segments spinning around a fixed pivot point, clockwise or counterclockwise depending on placement. Indestructible; damages on contact.

entities.name: Fire Bar (long)
entities.behavior: Extended Fire Bar variant; the World 5-4 fire bar in the original game is 12 fireball segments long (double the standard length). Same rotation and damage rules as the short variant.

entities.name: Piranha Plant
entities.behavior: Emerges from and retracts into vertical pipes, biting at the player. Deliberately will not emerge while the player is standing on or directly adjacent to its pipe. Cannot be stomped; only fireballs or Starman defeat it.
entities.palette_notes: Green head with yellow spots, orange stem.

entities.name: Bowser
entities.behavior: Final boss of each castle level (7 fakes before the real one in World 8-4). Walks, jumps, breathes fire, and throws hammers in later castles. Defeated by touching the Axe (drops the bridge, he falls in lava) or by 5 fireball hits.
entities.palette_notes: Original NES sprite: yellow hair, black eyebrows, grayish-blue body (not the now-standard red-haired design).
entities.confidence: verified behavior / size inferred / star-kill unverified

entities.name: Bowser Fire Breath
entities.behavior: Projectile fire attack breathed by Bowser toward the player during the boss encounter.
entities.confidence: inferred (page confirms fire-breathing behavior, no projectile-specific detail)

entities.name: Boo (You vs. Boo race mode)
entities.behavior: SMBD-exclusive race opponent in the 'You vs. Boo' bonus mode; does not appear as an in-level enemy. Does not damage the player on contact. Difficulty escalates through white, green, red, and finally a Black Boo that mimics the player's own best recorded time.
entities.palette_notes: White base color; green, red, and yellow-outlined black variants for higher difficulty tiers.

entities.name: Springboard / Jumping Board
entities.behavior: Bounces the player up and down when stood on; pressing jump at the peak of the bounce launches Mario extremely high. Appears in SMB1 Worlds 2-1, 3-1, 5-2, 6-3, 7-1, 8-2.
entities.palette_notes: Wooden board on a coiled base.

entities.name: Trampoline Floor (SMBD VS./Boo Race exclusive)
entities.behavior: Smaller SMBD-only variant of the Springboard used exclusively in VS. Game and You vs. Boo competitive modes.

entities.name: Platform - static wooden lift
entities.behavior: Non-moving wooden platform; visual style derived from the Donkey Kong 100m platforms.

entities.name: Platform - vertical moving lift
entities.behavior: Continuously moves up or down the screen, with new platforms dispensed from the opposite edge as old ones scroll off. First appears World 1-2.

entities.name: Platform - stationary oscillating lift
entities.behavior: Stays on screen while oscillating up and down in place, rather than scrolling off. Introduced World 1-3.

entities.name: Platform - horizontal moving lift
entities.behavior: Moves laterally back and forth across a fixed track. Introduced World 1-3.

entities.name: Platform - elevator lift
entities.behavior: Narrower paired platforms that scroll vertically off screen, similar to the vertical moving lift. Introduced World 2-4.

entities.name: Platform - balance (see-saw) lift
entities.behavior: Two platforms connected by a pulley; standing on one lowers it while raising the other. Both break and fall if overloaded. Introduced World 3-3.
entities.palette_notes: Brown wood plank texture, connected by a rope/pulley sprite.

entities.name: Platform - falling (flimsy) lift
entities.behavior: Sinks downward under the player's weight once stood on. Introduced World 3-3.

entities.name: Flagpole + Flag
entities.behavior: End-of-level goal. Contact height determines the score bonus. SMBD patches out the NES glitch that allowed vaulting clean over the pole.
entities.palette_notes: Bowser-emblem flag in the SMB1/SMBD era.

entities.name: Axe
entities.behavior: Touching it cuts the bridge Bowser stands on, dropping him into the lava below. Works regardless of whether Bowser was already defeated by fireballs (the bridge-drop animation just doesn't replay in that case).

entities.name: Coin
entities.behavior: Collectible pickup. 100 collected grants an extra life, a rule confirmed unchanged across SMB1, The Lost Levels, and SMB Deluxe.

entities.name: Red Coin (SMBD Challenge Mode)
entities.behavior: SMBD-only addition. 5 hidden per level in Challenge Mode; collecting all 5 earns the Red Coin Medal. Not present in the 1985 original.

entities.name: Yoshi Egg (SMBD Challenge Mode)
entities.behavior: SMBD-only addition. One hidden per Challenge Mode level, often stashed in a hidden block. Collecting it earns the Egg Medal. Not present in the 1985 original.
entities.confidence: must-verify (2000-pt figure from a secondary strategy guide, not a primary source)

entities.name: Super Mushroom
entities.behavior: Grows Small Mario into Super Mario. Slides at Mario's walking speed once released from a block, reversing direction on wall contact.
entities.palette_notes: NES original: yellow cap with red spots (not the later-standard red-cap/white-spot design).

entities.name: Fire Flower
entities.behavior: Grants Fire Mario, enabling fireball throws (max 2 on screen). Stationary item, does not slide like the Super Mushroom.
entities.palette_notes: 1985 original design: white petals, orange center, green stem/leaves.

entities.name: Super Star (Starman)
entities.behavior: Grants temporary invincibility to enemy contact (does not protect against pits, lava, or the timer). Consecutive-enemy-defeat scoring escalates while active.
entities.palette_notes: Yellow, five-pointed, with a simple face.
entities.confidence: verified core effect / chain-scoring exact values must-verify for SMB1 era

entities.name: 1-Up Mushroom
entities.behavior: Grants an extra life on contact.
entities.palette_notes: SMB1/SMBD-era palette: yellow-with-green-spots (overworld) or brown-with-teal-spots (underground); SMBD specifically updates this to the modern green-cap/white-spot design.

entities.name: Poison Mushroom
entities.behavior: NOT PRESENT in Super Mario Bros. or Super Mario Bros. Deluxe. First appeared in Super Mario Bros.: The Lost Levels (1986). Recorded here only as a documented roster omission.
entities.palette_notes: N/A - out of scope for SMB1/SMBD.

entities.name: Vine / Beanstalk
entities.behavior: Emerges and rapidly grows from a struck block, stopping at the first solid ceiling reached. Used to access secret areas such as Coin Heaven and Warp Zones.

entities.name: Warp Pipe
entities.behavior: Standard traversal/entry object. SMB1 pipes come in 4 colors: green (common), silver (castle/snow), orange, purple (rarest, warp zones). Some contain a Piranha Plant.

entities.name: Toad Rescue Message
entities.behavior: Scripted text-box cutscene shown after defeating the fake Bowser in Worlds 1-7's castles: a Toad says 'Thank you Mario! But our princess is in another castle!' Non-combat, no stats.

entities.name: Princess Peach Rescue Scene
entities.behavior: Scripted end-game cutscene after defeating the real Bowser in World 8-4: Princess Toadstool says 'Thank you Mario! Your quest is over. We present you a new quest.' Non-combat, no stats.

entities.name: Red Coin Medal (SMBD)
entities.behavior: Challenge Mode reward icon awarded when all 5 Red Coins in a level are collected. SMBD-exclusive.

entities.name: Egg Medal (SMBD)
entities.behavior: Challenge Mode reward icon awarded when the level's hidden Yoshi Egg is collected. SMBD-exclusive.

entities.name: High Score Medal (SMBD)
entities.behavior: Challenge Mode reward icon awarded when the player's score exceeds the level's preset Challenge Score. SMBD-exclusive.
